title: Course Schedule
source: DFS and BFS (Week 12): cycles in directed graphs

tests.name: Cycle in one part only
tests.hint: Courses 3, 4 and 5 form a cycle even though 0, 1 and 2 are fine.

tests.name: Random small
tests.data:
import random
random.seed(207)
cases = []
for _ in range(40):
    n = random.randint(1, 7)
    pairs = sorted({(random.randrange(n), random.randrange(n)) for _ in range(random.randint(0, 8))})
    cases.append((n, [list(p) for p in pairs]))
tests.expr: [can_finish(n, p) for n, p in cases]

tests.expr: can_finish(2000, [[i + 1, i] for i in range(1999)])
tests.hint: Recursive DFS goes 2 000 calls deep here, past Python's limit. Use Kahn's algorithm (a queue).

tests.name: A chain of 2 000 with a back edge
tests.expr: can_finish(2000, [[i + 1, i] for i in range(1999)] + [[0, 1999]])

tests.name: 2 000 courses, 5 000 pairs
tests.data:
import random
random.seed(2070)
order = list(range(2000))
random.shuffle(order)
pos = {c: i for i, c in enumerate(order)}
seen = set()
pairs = []
while len(pairs) < 5000:
    a, b = random.sample(range(2000), 2)
    if pos[b] < pos[a] and (a, b) not in seen:
        seen.add((a, b))
        pairs.append([a, b])
back_edge = [pairs[0][1], pairs[0][0]]
